comment: He is very kind and caring, and constantly checks in to see if you are correctly adjusting to the college lifestyle. The class is heavy in reading that is often unclear. Second half of the course is much more difficult than the first. The class is hard but rewarding. Plus, he has you over for brunch at his house.
I learned plenty from several of his classes. A great professor who will take the time to talk to you.
Go talk to him in his office.  He has a very offbeat way of thinking and communicating, but is so interesting to talk to one on one.  He'll go with pretty much anything so don't be shy.

Worst political bias I've seen in a professor.  Mutters comments about how "Republicans hate Native Americans."  Gives bad grades if you don't agree with him.  Extremely boring.  I'd quit school before I'd take another class with him.

Nelson is definitely not your ordinary English professor, but that's okay.  While he tends to lecture for long periods of time and constantly muses (mutters under his breath), he really knows what he's talking about if you can manage to follow it.  He does seem to want to help, but you'll have to be the one to ask for it.
Grading scale is uncomprehensible.  Very boring class but Nelson is extremely intelligent.  Always wears black jeans with brown belt and shoes...awesome
he grades most of the papers with check squigglees...

Rambles on and on, doesnt allow for much disscussion. Lectures on plot and expects you to do the analysis so many people can get away with not reading the books. Not many papers but is very inconsistent with grading. All in all, a very boring class. I end up counting down the minutes every time.
This professor is very very boring.  I learned absolutely nothing from his class.  He also is very unclear on grading... not good at all
He muses endlessly. But 40% of it is very important. Watch closely for the valuable nuggets. Monotone. Reserved.

Wow this guy sucks.  He is horrible at leading discussions.  He has no sense of voice projection and tends to get distracted [in a non-fun way].  He grades very sketchily...  it's always a surprise.  I didn't gain anything from his class

Though Nelson has a very unorganized way of leading discussion, he's very intelligent and is very willing to help and talk about paper topics. You can tell he loves what he's doing. Some classes were kind of boring, but I'm still glad I took the course.
